name: Half Dome via the Mist Trail
why: Past Vernal and Nevada Falls and up the last 120 m of bare granite on two steel cables to the top of Yosemite's symbol.
book: Permit needed when the cables are up (about Friday before Memorial Day to the day after the second Monday in October): preseason lottery in March, daily lottery two days before on recreation.gov. Free valley shuttle to Happy Isles.
water: Water at Vernal Fall footbridge; filter from the Merced River in Little Yosemite Valley. None above it: carry 4 litres.
dangers: Never climb the cables when the rock is wet or a storm is near: almost all fatal falls happened on wet rock.
Afternoon thunderstorms in summer: the summit is the highest point around.
A long day: many hikers run out of water.
turnaround: Be at the base of the cables by 13:30, or turn back.

points.name: Happy Isles trailhead
points.note: Shuttle stop 16, where the Mist Trail and the John Muir Trail start.

points.name: Vernal Fall
points.note: A 97 m waterfall; the Mist Trail climbs 600 granite steps beside it.

points.name: Nevada Fall
points.note: A 181 m fall below Liberty Cap; the trail crosses its top.

points.name: Sub Dome
points.note: Granite steps cut into the shoulder below the cables, with the ranger permit check.

points.name: Half Dome summit
points.note: A flat granite top 1,450 m above Yosemite Valley.
